references.text: God's original instructions to Moses on making the menorah with its utensils and lamps, as referenced in Exodus 35:14.
Instructions regarding the pure, pressed olive oil for the menorah, corresponding to the 'oil for the lampstand' mentioned in the verse.
Bezalel carries out the work of making the menorah and its utensils, fulfilling the instructions in Exodus 35:14.
Listing of the finished menorah with its lamps and oil as part of the tabernacle's furnishings.
God commands Moses to place the menorah in the tabernacle and light the lamps.
Further instructions regarding the oil for the menorah and Aaron's responsibility to tend the lamps.
Instructions to Aaron on lighting the seven lamps on the menorah.
The Epistle to the Hebrews describes the furnishings of the tabernacle, including the menorah, as a shadow of heavenly things.
John sees seven golden lampstands in his vision, linking back to the tabernacle's menorah as a symbol of God's presence.
The seven lamps burning before the throne, identified as the seven spirits of God, reflect the symbolism of the menorah.
Connects God's specific requirement (25:6) with the people's concrete delivery (35:14), demonstrating perfect obedience.
Contains the same list of materials and describes the same collection event as the source verse.
Confirms that the oil for the menorah was a central part of the collection effort in the same chapter.
Links the need for oil for lighting with the holy handling of the menorah during transport.
Affirms the menorah's role as an integrated unit with all its utensils within the structure of the sanctuary.
Confirms that the menorah with all its accessories was an integral part of God's original design.
